entries.topic: FBI cases: 1940s to Pollard, Kadish, AIPAC/Franklin; counterintelligence findings and denials

claims.text: Wikipedia: 1940s Haganah procurement despite US embargo; FBI investigations produced a few convictions; Marshall complained in 1948 Israeli delegates knew Truman's instructions 'almost as soon' as sent; 1954 FBI found Israeli intelligence had cultivated sources in the US government.

Green (CSM 1989): in 1956 an Israeli official offered payment to US Embassy official Earl Jensen, who cooperated under FBI and DOJ guidance; the two Israeli contacts were apparently not prosecuted; Col. Yosef Langotsky (assistant army attaché) entered secure Pentagon areas 1976–79 and was recalled in early 1979 after DoD cut his access; in 1969 on FBI recommendations NUMEC lost contracts and its president's clearances were lifted.

McConnell (1986): FBI arrested Pollard on 21 Nov 1985 outside the Israeli embassy where he sought asylum; arraigned six days later; Pollard run by LEKEM (LAKAM) under Rafi Eitan; Richard Kelly Smyth indicted May 1985 for shipping krytrons to Israel; 1978 Senate Intelligence Committee study: FBI investigated friendly services only on specific complaints and information rarely reached prosecutors.

CSM (1986): Israel said the Pollard operation was unauthorized; some Reagan administration officials doubted that, citing court documents showing an organized, well-financed ring involving Israeli officers and embassy staff.

CIA damage assessment (30 Oct 1987): Pollard compromised about 800 documents and ~1,500 messages; taskings on Arab states, Pakistan and the USSR; Israelis 'never expressed interest in US military activities, plans, capabilities, or equipment'; handler Yagur told Pollard to ignore a request for 'dirt' on Israeli officials.

Wikipedia (well-established): Pollard pleaded guilty and was sentenced to life in 1987; Israel formally apologized in 1987 and pledged no further spying on US soil; paroled 2015; emigrated to Israel in 2020 after parole expired, welcomed personally by Netanyahu. Kadish admitted passing classified material to an Israeli agent 1979–1985; in 2009, aged 85, he was fined under a plea deal with no jail (NYT). Franklin pleaded guilty in 2005, sentenced to 12 years, later reduced; DOJ dropped Espionage Act charges against Rosen and Weissman in 2009.
1996 GAO report: Israel 'conducts the most aggressive espionage operation against the United States of any US ally' (as quoted).

A Defense Department memo (reported by the LA Times in 1996) labelled Israel a 'non-traditional adversary' and suggested it used ties to American Jews; after it leaked it was quickly disavowed by the Pentagon.

Politico (12 Sep 2019), per three former officials: IMSI-catcher devices found near the White House and other sensitive sites; FBI and DHS forensic analysis linked them to Israeli agents; no public rebuke; Israel called it a 'blatant lie'; Trump said he found it hard to believe. (Wikipedia summary of Politico, Guardian and Times of Israel; original not retrieved.)

June 2026: the DIA reportedly raised its counterintelligence threat assessment for Israel to 'critical', over concern Israel was surveilling senior US officials on Middle East decision-making, per NBC News, Times of Israel and NYT as summarized by Wikipedia; originals not retrieved.
